question: If an agency is using an approved retroreflectivity-management method but a few individual signs temporarily fall below Table 2A-5, is the agency automatically out of compliance? Include the white-on-red thresholds relevant to STOP-type signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The Standard requires the agency to use an assessment or management method designed to maintain retroreflectivity at or above the Table 2A-5 minimums; the accompanying Support text explicitly states that an agency using such a method remains in compliance even if some individual signs are below the minimums at a particular point in time. For white-on-red signs such as STOP signs, Table 2A-5 requires maintained levels of white ≥ 35 and red ≥ 7 cd/lx/m² (at 0.2° observation and −4.0° entrance angles), with a minimum sign contrast ratio of at least 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity). Standards (mandatory): - "Public agencies or officials having jurisdiction shall use an assessment or management method that is designed to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5." Guidance (recommended): - Except for signs identified in Paragraph 5, one or more of the methods described in "Maintaining Traffic Sign Retroreflectivity" (FHWA-SA-07-020, Revised 2013), or a method developed based on an engineering study, should be used to maintain retroreflectivity at or above the Table 2A-5 minimums, and "Signs that are identified through the agency’s method as being below the minimum levels should be replaced." Options (permitted): - Highway agencies may exclude the following from the retroreflectivity maintenance guidelines: Parking, Standing, and Stopping (R7 and R8 series) signs; Walking/Hitchhiking/Crossing (R9 series, R10-1 through R10-4b) signs; Acknowledgment signs; and Bikeway signs intended for exclusive use by bicyclists or pedestrians. Support (explanatory): - "Compliance with the Standard in Paragraph 2 of this Section is achieved by having a method in place and using the method... an agency or official having jurisdiction would be in compliance with the Standard in Paragraph 2 of this Section even if there are some individual signs that do not meet the minimum retroreflectivity levels at a particular point in time." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2A-5, "Minimum Maintained Retroreflectivity Levels," which lists the white-on-red row (W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7 for all sheeting types) and footnote 4 requiring a minimum sign contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity), the criteria applicable to STOP-type signs. Citations: - Section 2A.22 Standard §2 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Support §3 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Guidance §4 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Option §5 (p.63) - Table 2A-5 (p.62)
gold_answer: Not automatically. The agency complies by having and using a method designed to maintain the minimums, even if some individual signs fall below them at a particular moment. For white on red, the table gives white at least 35, red at least 7 cd/lx/m², and at least a 3:1 white-to-red contrast ratio.
